title: Morphological Principles of Augmentation (Al-Mazīd)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 19; Ryding Ch. 20 §§20.1–20.2)
objectives: Understand how prefixation, infixation, and gemination modify triliteral root meanings.
Identify the predictable participle prefixes (مُـ) for derived Forms II–X.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 6: What three consonants represent the schematic triliteral root?

sections.heading: Systematic Root Augmentation
sections.body: From a single triliteral root (Form I), Arabic derives up to nine common augmented stems (Forms II–X) by doubling a radical, lengthening a vowel, or adding prefixes/infixes. Each form carries characteristic semantic tendencies (causative, reflexive, reciprocal, passive, or desiderative) and has completely predictable maṣādir and participles.

sections.label: Derived Participles Rule
sections.summary: For ALL derived forms (II–X), replace the imperfect prefix with مُـ: kasrah before the final radical forms the Active Participle (مُعَلِّمٌ 'teacher'), and fatḥah before the final radical forms the Passive Participle (مُعَلَّمٌ 'taught').

sections.translation: he knew → he taught → he learned
sections.irab: الجَذْرُ: ع-ل-م | عَلِمَ (١) | عَلَّمَ (٢: تَعْدِيَةٌ) | تَعَلَّمَ (٥: مُطَاوَعَةٌ)
sections.notes: One root (ع-ل-م) yields 'to know' (Form I), 'to cause to know / teach' (Form II), and 'to learn' (Form V).

sections.heading: Use the Verb-Form Explorer
sections.body: You can compare all ten forms side-by-side anytime in Grammar Tools → Verb Forms I–X.
